material_findings: capability assessment and stage ordering were incomplete
actual provider selection was not cleanly EVF-owned
execution-runtime and Lean theorem paths were not closed end to end
validation parsed schemas without executing semantic fixtures
acceptance and currentness coherence was incomplete
ordinary provider evidence did not directly bind its exact runtime
bounded PASS and current FormalClaim refs could contradict their currentness assertions
a bounded-PASS case package did not require an exact current EVF join

closed_findings.conclusion: Capability assessment is an explicit S4 artifact and a preservation-backed projection precedes executable TDE derivation.
TDE owns derivation and provider-routing candidates; EVF owns actual provider selection and evidence routing.
Execution evidence directly binds its exact runtime, and execution-obligation and theorem-request routes are explicit alternatives through provider evidence and EVF join.
The validator executes 50 positive and negative semantic fixtures over 16 schemas and requires the exact currentness and runtime regression cases.
Current FormalClaims require current semantic refs, bounded PASS requires every route ref current, and bounded-PASS case packages require one exact current EVF join.

claim_ceiling: Candidate schema, ontology, fixture, and static-validation closure only. This review proves no provider execution, theorem, EVF operational PASS, runtime conformance, business claim, release, deployment, or production readiness.
